title: The `^` operator: no operator-side row count exists anywhere in OxFunc
status_plain: `^` and POWER bind the same kernel (`FUNC_ID_OP_POWER => power_kernel`), and the claim sentences name the operator. But every counted row in the POWER lane is a `=POWER(A1, B1)` worksheet call: there is no `^` column, no `^` row count, and the W108 plan's B3 operator sweep was never executed (no `w108-b3` run directory exists). The operator therefore inherits POWER's warrant without a measurement of its own. Its only operator-specific Excel evidence is uncounted -- three math-deviation entries, all on a different Excel build (20026) from POWER's sign-off build (20131).

counts.build_note: XMD-004, XMD-008 and XMD-009 -- the only entries carrying operator-specific witnesses -- cite live Excel build 20026, a different build from POWER's 20131 sign-off. None publishes a count.
counts.corpus_or_build: POWER worksheet calls only; no operator corpus exists
counts.ambiguity_note: The mechanism of the inheritance is a shared kernel, confirmed in code at surface_dispatch.rs:2934. The only in-repo joint check is a single-row unit test asserting 0^0 -> #NUM! for both ids.
counts.source_sentence: `POWER(x, y)` (and `x ^ y`) for a **fractional exponent with a positive base** currently calls `f64::powf` (UCRT).

ruled_out: a dedicated operator kernel: OP_POWER and POWER both bind `power_kernel`
open_question: Whether Excel's `^` operator and its POWER function publish identical bits has never been measured. The W108 plan named the sweep (B3) and it was not run.
reader_warning: POWER's 715/715 is not the operator's result. It is a count of POWER worksheet calls, and this record credits `^` with no count.
